newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Puts sold in Halifax, GEC.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Puts sold in Halifax, GEC.

text.p: Options in Halifax Plc, the recently floated bank and GEC Plc, the electronics group, were among the more active UK stock options on Tuesday, dealers said.

The main deals came from put options sellers hoping the underlying shares would stay above the strike price in order to capture the options premium or to acquire the underlying shares if they fell below the strike price when the puts could be assigned, they said.
In Halifax, the largest bargain was a seller of 2,500 October 750 puts at 40p. And in GEC, there was a seller of 1,000 August 330 puts at 10p.
At 1315 GMT, Halifax shares were 15p up at 764p while GEC added 12-1/2p to 349p.
Elsewhere, volatility trades -- through straddles and strangles -- were the chief deals in insurers Prudential Corporation Plc and Royal & Sun Alliance Plc.
In Prudential, the long straddle consisted of 250 August 700 puts and calls bought at 62p and 17p each, which will make money at expiry if the shares either trade below 621p or above 779p.
In Royal & Sun Alliance the main deal was a long strangle established by buying 250 July 460 puts at 6-1/2p along with 250 July 500 calls at 11-1/2p.
Shares in Royal & Sun Alliance gained 6p to 486-1/2p while Prudential was 2p better at 653p.
One of the larger deals in FTSE 100 index options was the sale of 1,400 June 4800 calls at about 13p which will make a maximum profit of 13p if the FTSE stays below 4,800 by expiry.
By 1315 GMT cash FTSE was up 17.7 at 4,704.4 and June FTSE futures were up 13 at 4,722
